topic: Can the proposed FPA illumination uniformity handle dynamic beam reconfiguration without compromising network throughput during peak congestion?
consensus_response: The proposed FPA illumination uniformity is compromised by dynamic beam reconfiguration due to increased interference between adjacent beams. The array factor, which steers beams, introduces additional interference when adapting to changing traffic demands. This can lead to reduced capacity (40% gains) and degraded illumination uniformity. However, leveraging machine learning-based adaptive beamforming can mitigate these trade-offs by learning and adapting to changing traffic patterns in real-time. Nevertheless, the complexity of this approach may introduce additional interference and degrade illumination uniformity, requiring careful design and optimization.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of dynamic beam reconfiguration on FPA illumination uniformity, including increased co-channel interference (CCI) and reduced capacity. It also discusses various techniques for managing interference, such as orthogonal frequency reuse, semi-orthogonal frequency reuse, and full frequency reuse.
